509.t: Abart's trio with Louis Powers and Harold Minor
509.s: She took a trio to Abart's on 9th Street for about a year, and fumbles the dates.
509.q: Well, no, that was the beginning, and then there‘s a place called . . . on 9th Street . . . Abart‘s [phonetic]. We had done 7-T, so let me go in and check that. I just went there and same thing, and the mom and dad liked me, and they were building this place. And I said, ―I‘d like to have the job.‖…

509.t: The Bohemian Caverns trio and the grueling hours
509.s: With Stump Saunders and Louis Powers she played long weekly hours at the Bohemian Caverns she calls slavery time.
509.q: See, at that time I had—I want to say this for the guys—I had the baddest trio then. Number one, I was right out of school. I was, I mean, my chops were . . . I was so strong, and I was trying to . . . I‘m trying to get into jazz, and I‘m still with the classics. I was just bad. I mean, I was…

509.t: Taking the band at the 7-T Cocktail Lounge
509.s: Next to the Howard Theater she won a job at the 7-T by being young and cute, leading a quintet that played How High the Moon.
509.q: Yes. But you know one thing? I just said, ―Let me go in, too. I‘m going to do it my way.‖ You going to wait for me? Oh, keep going? Anyway, there‘s a place called 7­ T [Seventy?] Cocktail Lounge, and let‘s see, before that I used to try to in and sit in with the guys. I just wanted to learn, you…

509.t: Olivia's Patio Lounge and opening for the big stars
509.s: Olivia's was the biggest room in Washington, where her trio opened for Oscar Peterson and the Modern Jazz Quartet.
509.q: Oh, child, that was great. Olivia‘s Patio Lounge was the biggest thing to come to Washington, and I‘m trying to think of the year. But a long time before that she had a place called . . . a place, and I had changed my age to play there. It was called . . . what‘s

367.t: Gerald's Detroit bands and the Plantation Club
367.s: Gerald played with Hal Green, Gloster Current and the Plantation Club band in Detroit, then joined Chick Carter's band where he met Snooky; they argue over 1938 or 1939.

65.t: Working with Mulato's Three Habaneros at the Mella Club
65.s: He returned to music with Mulato at the Mella Club in Harlem, then a trip to Detroit.
65.ch: Arriving in New York and founding the Afro-Cubans
65.q: Well, I always was enthusiastic about to organize something, so I start working with Mulato with the Three Habaneros, at the Mella Club.

380.s: He worked at the club in the Majestic Hotel around 1935 until his father took him home.
380.ch: Youth, the road and arrival in California
380.q: I mentioned the Majestic Hotel. Well, there was a nightclub in the hotel called Henry's Furnace, and I... I know I'm mixing my times up here, because this was the second time when I'd come back to Cleveland, that I got hired to work in this place.

90.t: The Congo Club and Big Nick
90.s: The Congo Club in the Norwood Hotel, where he joined the house band and Big Nick encouraged him.
90.q: The Congo Club was located in the Norwood(?) Hotel, 555 East Adams Boulevard. It was like... East Adams Street, yeah. It was like the place. Slim Jenkins was the owner, and downstairs in the Norwood(?) Hotel, they had this very fine club, and it was called the Congo Club. Now, the Congo Club...…

383.t: Why Detroit: summers hearing the big traveling bands
383.s: An aunt in Detroit hosted the boys in summers, where Wilson heard McKinney's Cotton Pickers, Fletcher Henderson, Jimmy Noone and Horace Henderson at the Greystone.
383.q: Well, Detroit came in the picture because I had an aunt and an uncle living in Detroit -- my mother's ... one of her younger sisters who had -- one that was very close to her, one who had helped her in Austin, Texas, when I was born, this sister came out to Austin, Texas to help her with me and my…

72.t: Havana, then quitting in Detroit and forming a band at the Savoy
72.s: After Cuba he left the show in Detroit and led a seven-piece band at the Savoy for about six months (Welburn's note: Chilton dates it 1927-28).
72.q: Then I left Benbow... I left the theatre and got with Benbow. Then I went all down through the South. I ended up going to Havana -- Havana, Cuba.

386.t: Train mishap and landing at Detroit's Club Harlem
386.s: He is put off a Toronto train in Michigan and then goes to Detroit, where the Club Harlem hires him for 1933-37.
386.q: '33, I think it was. I decided that...this guy came from Toronto and he had a ticket, a return ticket to Toronto. And he didn't want to go back to Toronto and he gave me the ticket. Well in those days it wasn't as easy to try to get from one...you know, like this man would accept you on your honest…

235.t: Other Detroit clubs and leaving after a year and a half
235.s: He names the Three Sixes and El Zino, says he stayed about eighteen months, then went straight to Earl Hines.
235.q: Yeah. There was the Three Sixes and there was a late club up the street, I forget the name of that...where we could go jam and, oh let's see...oh there were several places there where you could go hear other musicians play so it was a nice atmosphere. Of course the Club Congo was it and then the…

169.t: Tubby Hayes' sextet in Detroit; why his father left Detroit
169.s: He works in Detroit with a six-piece band at River Rouge; an aside on the 1920s when his father was laid off in Detroit.
169.q: So I stayed with him until I got a job in Detroit working with a six-piece band. I think his name was Hayes, a tenor player -- Tubby, they called him. Not Tubby Hayes. This is Tubby we called him. And he had a guy named Johnny something who played piano, and Freddie Radcliff played the drums...

6.t: Christmas 1928 with McKinney's Cotton Pickers in Detroit
6.s: Using a downBeat article he wrote as notes, he recounts being recommended by Benny Carter to McKinney, earning $160 a week, and returning home after two weeks homesick.
6.ch: Early records, Detroit and Prohibition-era nightlife
6.q: Well, you see, there's a break there, in the -- Christmas, 1928, I was out in Detroit with McKinney's Cotton Pickers. I went out there and -- hand me that envelope there, please. I don't want to get up because I've got this -- I brought my -- I figured I'd need this. This is a thing I wrote for…

124.s: His brothers recruit Baltimore musicians for a band and invite him to Atlantic City; William arranged and played piano, Floyd played alto.
124.ch: Philadelphia and the McRae Brothers Band, 1908-1929
124.q: to be your double. The double on the flute didn't come till later and I never did get to (inaudible) the flute. I went to the bass clarinet. My double was bass. Was a E-flat (inaudible) soprano, bass clarinet, tenor, bass sax and alto. When we -- my brother built his band and decided when they were…
